learning: The forward offset trades oval progress against s-bend progress. Line loss stays at one event per run on oval and s-bend, and the controller does not remove it. Any remaining gain would need per-track loss-point telemetry or a controller change tested on the development tracks, which this final iteration cannot do.
notes: Final design: the iteration 9 geometry (y 0.06 m) with its paired controller, unchanged. Every value is inside the contract limits.
rationale: Iteration 9 is the best measured design (52.985), reproduced exactly in iteration 10. Moving the five 12 mm sensors from y 0.05 to 0.06 m raised oval progress from 0.138 to 0.151 and oval score from 56.25 to 62.77. S-bend progress fell from 0.148 to 0.140, and slalom was unchanged at 0.097. Line loss stayed at one event per run on oval and s-bend and at two on slalom. Steering oscillation stayed between 0.10 and 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. Because this is the final iteration and the unseen track has no race evidence, I commit the measured best design and keep its paired controller unchanged. I do not interpolate to y 0.055 m, since an untested offset could lose the measured oval gain. Geometry and controller are therefore identical to iteration 9, and the expected result is about 52.99.
